plan_draft.title: Markdown‑to‑PDF CLI Tool Plan
plan_draft.overview: Create a command‑line utility that reads a Markdown file, converts it to HTML, and renders a styled PDF with a table of contents. The tool uses click for the CLI, markdown for parsing, and WeasyPrint for PDF generation.

phases.title: Project setup and dependencies
phases.body:
Create a new directory and `python -m venv .venv`.
Activate the venv and run `pip install click weasyprint markdown`.
Create a `src/` package and add an empty `__init__.py`.
Add a `pyproject.toml` with minimal metadata.
Pin Python version >=3.10 to satisfy WeasyPrint's requirement[^weasyprint-1].
Initialize a git repository.

phases.title: CLI skeleton with click
phases.body:
Create `src/cli.py`.
Import `click` and decorate a `main` function with `@click.command()`[^click-1].
Add `@click.argument('input_path', type=click.Path(exists=True))` and `@click.argument('output_path', type=click.Path())`.
Add optional `--css` option using `@click.option('--css', type=click.Path())`[^click-2].
Inside `main`, call a `convert(input_path, output_path, css_path)` helper.
Add `if __name__ == '__main__': main()`.

phases.title: Markdown to HTML conversion
phases.body:
In `src/convert.py`, import the `markdown` package[^markdown-1].
Read the markdown file into a string.
Convert the string to HTML using the library's conversion function (API not detailed in brief).
If a CSS path is provided, embed a `<link>` tag or `<style>` block in the HTML.
Return the final HTML string.
Write unit tests that verify HTML contains expected tags.

phases.title: PDF generation with WeasyPrint
phases.body:
Import `HTML` from `weasyprint`[^weasyprint-1].
Create an `HTML` object with the HTML string: `doc = HTML(string=html_content)`.
Call `doc.write_pdf(output_path)` to produce the PDF.
Ensure only a single HTML input is passed (multiple inputs raise an error)[^weasyprint-2].
Catch and report any WeasyPrint exceptions.
Add a test that checks the PDF file is created and non‑empty.

phases.title: Table of contents integration
phases.body:
Research WeasyPrint's support for automatic TOC (not covered in briefs).
If supported, add appropriate CSS/HTML markers to generate TOC.
Otherwise, prepend a manually built TOC based on markdown headings (requires parsing headings, not detailed in briefs).
Document the chosen approach and any limitations.
Update `convert` to include the TOC before PDF rendering.
Add tests for presence of TOC entries in the PDF.

phases.title: Packaging and verification
phases.body:
Add an entry point in `pyproject.toml`: `markdown-pdf = "src.cli:main"`.
Run `pip install -e .` and test the CLI with sample files.
Verify that running `markdown-pdf sample.md out.pdf` produces a styled PDF with TOC.
Check that the tool fails gracefully on missing files or invalid CSS.
Update README with usage instructions.
Commit all changes.

pitfalls: WeasyPrint requires Python 3.10+; using older versions will cause import errors.
WeasyPrint's public API may change without notice, potentially breaking `HTML` usage.
Passing multiple inputs to `HTML` raises an error; ensure only one HTML string is supplied.
The markdown library's exact conversion function is not specified in the brief; verify the correct API.
Click option parsing can misinterpret file paths containing spaces; quote arguments when invoking.
Large markdown files may consume significant memory when held as a single string.
